Quanto a raquete pesa de fábrica, sem co: How much the racket weighs as sold, unstrung and without an overgrip. Strings add about 15 to 18 g (0.5 to 0.6 oz). More weight brings stability and a heavier ball; less weight makes it easier to handle but sends more shock to the arm.
O quanto a raquete “pesa” quando você ba: How heavy the racket “feels” when you swing it. It's measured in a lab, and it's what you feel on the shot, more than the weight on a scale. Up to 310: quick and easy. 315 to 325: balanced. Above 325: a heavier ball and more stability, but more tiring, and you may swing late.
Ponto de equilíbrio medido a partir do f: The balance point measured from the butt of the handle, in mm. Below about 320 mm (unstrung) the racket is head-light: quick at the net with more control. Above that, it's head-heavy: easy power, but harder on the wrist.
O quanto o quadro dobra no impacto, numa: How much the frame flexes on impact, on a scale of about 55 to 72. A stiffer frame returns more energy, so more power. Up to 63 is usually described as more comfortable for players with arm issues; the link to injury hasn't been proven.
Área do aro em polegadas quadradas (pol²: The area of the hoop in square inches (sq in). 97 to 98: more precision. 100: the middle ground for most players. 102 or more: a bigger sweet spot and more pop.
Verticais × horizontais. Aberto (16×19,: Mains × crosses. An open pattern (16×19, 16×18) bites the ball more: more spin and more pop. A dense pattern (18×20) gives more control and strings last longer.
Facilidade de a bola sair com profundida: How easily the ball goes deep without you swinging harder. It comes from a bigger head, a stiffer frame and a higher swingweight.
Previsibilidade da bola: ela vai onde vo: How predictable the ball is: it goes where you aim. It comes from a smaller head, a denser pattern, a more flexible frame and more mass.
Facilidade de gerar efeito. Vem de padrã: How easily you can put spin on the ball. It comes from an open pattern, a bigger head and enough swingweight to accelerate the ball.
O quanto a raquete tende a ser confortáv: How comfortable the racket tends to feel at contact. It comes mainly from a flexible frame, enough mass and a head-light balance; dampening technologies count for little.
Facilidade de mover a raquete rápido: na: How easily you can move the racket fast: at the net, on returns and late in a match. It comes from a lower swingweight and weight.
O quanto a raquete segura contra bola pe: How well the racket holds up against heavy shots and mishits without twisting. It comes from more mass and swingweight.
Índice nosso, de 0 a 10, que combina rig: Our own index, from 0 to 10, combining stiffness, weight and balance (dampening technology counts for little). The higher it is, the more comfortable the racket tends to be for the elbow, shoulder and wrist. No racket prevents or treats an injury; if the pain persists, see a doctor or other health professional.
Nota de 0 a 100% que mede o encaixe da r: A score from 0 to 100% that measures how well the racket fits your game. We compare the racket with your ideal profile and take into account your body, your arm, your budget and what you want to gain from the switch.
Força com que a corda é esticada, em lib: How tightly the strings are pulled, in pounds (lb). Lower: more power and comfort, less control. Higher: more control, a shorter ball and more vibration. Poly is usually strung 2 to 4 lb lower than multifilament.
Escala americana de nível, de 1.0 a 7.0,: The USTA rating system, from 1.0 to 7.0. 2.5: rallies slowly. 3.0: consistent at medium pace. 3.5: directs the ball and starts coming to the net. 4.0: dependable strokes and varied spin. 4.5 or higher: uses power and spin as weapons, strong serve. If in doubt, pick the lower level. If you only know your UTR, go by the descriptions.
O tamanho e a velocidade do movimento at: The length and speed of your swing to the ball. Short and compact: the racket travels little before contact, common for players who block the ball or play at the net. Long and fast: a big take-back and strong acceleration, like the pros.
Além das specs medidas, cada raquete com: Beyond the measured specs, every racket with reviews published on major sites (Tennis Warehouse, Tennisnerd, Tennis Companion and others) has its profile adjusted by the playtesters' consensus. We look at where it's strong or weak, not just the overall score, because a tester who likes a racket tends to rate everything high. Playtester approval also counts in the DNA Score, because it helps predict whether you'll enjoy the racket.
Os profissionais assinam uma linha, mas: Pros endorse a line, but almost always play custom versions: heavier, with lead tape, sometimes an older frame with the current paint job. The retail model is the closest thing, not the same racket. Use it as a style reference, not as proof that it suits you.
A espessura do cabo, de L1 a L5 (4 1/8 a: Handle thickness, from L1 to L5 (4 1/8 to 4 5/8 inches). A handle that fits your hand lets you hold it without squeezing, which is usually more comfortable; too big locks up your wrist.
